messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p95 latency spike detected for /v1/generate (hosted) — current p95 1.9s (SLO 1.0s), p99 3.6s. 3.4x baseline. triggered at 2026-03-12T15:12:02Z

incident-bot: linked alerts: kv_cache_evictions/sec ↑, stream_stalls ↑, worker_queue_depth ↑, correlated with model: redwood-open-l7 (quantized)

devon: paging — I'm oncall. I see the page, looking now.

sanjay: @devon do we have customer impact yet? any streaming sessions stalled?

devon: yes, streaming stalls intermittently. A few calls hit tail decode times ~6-8s. Not global, concentrated on region-us-west2 and a couple of dedicated pools.

maria: grabbing dashboard: p95 by region shows spike starting ~15:08Z, p99 more noisy. KV cache hitrate dropped from 0.95 -> 0.68. evictions/sec jumped.

kevin: jumping in — that pattern smells like cache fragmentation or eviction pressure. We recently enabled aggressive prefill for chat sessions to reduce cold-start for long contexts. Could be prefill writes evicting active decode KV entries.

lina: confirmed: trace sampling shows prefill RPCs write large KV prefixes right before a running decode for other requests, leading to cache churn. decode tries to fetch keys, misses, falls back to recompute -> stall.

devon: ok immediate mitigations we can do in order: 1) temporarily disable prefill feature flag for hosted region-us-west2 2) raise KV cache soft limit for affected pools 3) enable targeted routing to fallback smaller-quant models for non-SLA customers 4) roll restart a few actors to defragment sharded cache if needed

sanjay: please do step 1 now; that's fastest. @maria can you toggle the flag for region-us-west2 and confirm? include rollback steps.

maria: doing it now. Patch: POST /api/flags/set {"flag":"prefill_write_enabled","region":"us-west2","value":false} 

maria: response 200. Flag set false. Propagating in 30s across control plane.

ops-bot: CONTROLPLANE: flag change observed: prefill_write_enabled=false for region-us-west2 (triggered by maria).

devon: watching metrics. KV evictions/sec trending down already. p95 dropping from 1.9s -> 1.2s within 90s. p99 still elevated but improving.

kevin: good. longer-term we need to rebalance prefill vs decode writes: reduce prefill batch size, or write to a separate prefill namespace with lower eviction priority, or pre-warm without writing KV if decode-friendly.

lina: added a short runbook note to incident: "prefill_vs_kv_runbook" with checklist. recommend param changes: prefill_max_keys_per_req=256 -> 64, prefill_write_ttl=600, kv_priority=low for prefill.

devon: next action: raise soft cache limit for affected pools by 20% as a safety. @kevin can you apply to dedicated-pool-usw2-1? command: `rdctl pool update --id dedicated-pool-usw2-1 --kv-soft-limit-percent +20`

kevin: running now. CLI shows pending. Applying to two subpools serially to avoid spike.

kevin: update: applied to dedicated-pool-usw2-1 and dedicated-pool-usw2-2. Cache pressure easing. p95 ~0.98s now. p99 ~1.8s.

devon: looks like disabling prefill + increasing kv soft limit bought us stable tail. We should keep prefill disabled for a controlled rollout of the safer prefill params.

maria: notifying customer-success for impacted customers. CS-bot: tagging accounts with requests in last 15m.

sanjay: assignment: devon own incident. kevin and lina support on config changes. maria coordinate CS comms. open incident ticket and severity => SEV2.

devon: created incident ticket INC-2026-0312-73. Added timeline and actions.

lina: noted possible root cause: prefill->writes are larger than expected and cause eviction hot-spots when combined with high concurrency decode. Key fragmentation across shards makes eviction uneven. We'll need a follow-up: compact keys, add stronger LRU per-shard, consider evict-aware prefill backpressure.

kevin: one more datapoint: heap usage on runtime nodes also transiently increased during prefill bursts, GC contributed to stalls. so both memory and KV eviction interact.

devon: immediate postmortem actions: 1) revert prefill change once safe param rollout is tested in staging 2) add an automated protection: if kv_evictions/sec > X and p99 > Y then throttle prefill writes (circuit-breaker) 3) instrument per-key TTL and shard eviction heatmap 4) customer impact report and post-incident review within 48h.

maria: CS notified customers A,B,C with short note. No SLA credits requested yet but CS tracking.

devon: closing loop: current status — incident mitigated, p95 within SLO, p99 trending down. Keeping incident open for monitoring for 4h. Will do handoff to next oncall at 16:00Z.

sanjay: thanks all. @devon take a formal handoff at 16:00Z and post a short update then.

devon: will do. I'll draft the incident summary and add follow-up tickets: #FV-237 (prefill tuning), #INF-882 (kv eviction dashboard), #OPS-119 (circuit-breaker).

incident-bot: NOTE: This thread will be tagged as "incident: in-progress". Use /incident close when done.

devon: tagging final note before handoff: if anyone sees p99 > 2s after 16:00Z escalate to pagers.

kevin: ack.

lina: ack and saving traces to /traces/INC-2026-0312-73 for postmortem.
